texts: When cold wind blows off the sea at night, the cold wind extinguishes unprepared lanterns.
If cold wind strikes the Cliff Path at night, unprepared lanterns go out.
Lanterns in shielded coves stay safe from cold winds.

parse_run2: (: wind_extinguish_lantern_rule (Implication (And (Member $x wind) (Member $x cold) (Member $y lantern) (Member $y unprepared)) (And (Member (sk_extinguish $x $y) extinguish) (Agent (sk_extinguish $x $y) $x) (Patient (sk_extinguish $x $y) $y))) (STV 0.9 0.9))

q1_issues.issue: Both arguments are bare kind-denoting plurals, which the relational-generic rule routes to an opaque kind-level relation; the emitted per-instance all-pairs rule is exactly the 'distributing it to all instance-pairs' the instruction set warns against, asserting that every cold wind extinguishes every unprepared lantern anywhere.

q2_gaps: a relational generic whose kind NPs carry non-fusing descriptive modifiers ('cold winds', 'unprepared lanterns') - the both-arguments-bare-kind trigger fires, but the compound rules forbid fusing an incidental descriptive adjective into a kind symbol, so there is no licensed single kind term to put in the relation's two argument slots
review_run1.notes: Splitting 'cold' and 'unprepared' off as separate Member properties on the instance variables is correct (incidental description, not a fusing classifier), 'unprepared' is rightly a positive property rather than a negation, and Agent on the inanimate transitive subject follows the rule.

fields.sentence: When cold wind blows off the sea at night, the cold wind extinguishes unprepared lanterns.
parse_run2: (: wind_extinguish_rule (Implication (And (Member $x wind) (Member $x cold) (Member (sk_blow $x) blow) (Patient (sk_blow $x) $x) (Source (sk_blow $x) sk_sea_1) (Time (sk_blow $x) night)) (And (Member (sk_extinguish $x) extinguish) (Agent (sk_extinguish $x) $x) (Patient (sk_extinguish $x) unprepared_lantern) (During (sk_extinguish $x) (sk_blow $x)))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

q1_issues.issue: The rule's premise builds the trigger event as a Skolem-function term — (Member (sk_blow $x) blow) (Agent (sk_blow $x) $x) — instead of the bare event variable every worked antecedent uses, so the premise cannot match an ordinary asserted blowing event and the rule is unfireable.

The intransitive subject of "blows" is given Agent, but wind is a non-volitional natural force (a gas in motion), which the intransitive-subject test routes to Patient alongside "smoke rose" and "the tide receded".

review_run1.notes: The rest is right: "cold" and "unprepared" are left unfused as separate Member atoms on the individuals, Source carries "off the sea", night is the bare day-part symbol on Time, the transitive inanimate extinguisher keeps Agent, and During ties the response to its trigger.

fields.sentence: If cold wind strikes the Cliff Path at night, unprepared lanterns go out.
parse_run2: (: windstrike_lantern_rule (Implication (And (Member $x strike) (Agent $x $w) (Member $w wind) (Member $w cold) (Theme $x cliff_path) (Time $x night) (Member $l lantern) (Member $l unprepared)) (And (Member (sk_go_out $x $l) go_out) (Patient (sk_go_out $x $l) $l) (During (sk_go_out $x $l) $x))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

q1_issues.issue: The antecedent's wind and striking are written as constants sk_wind_1 / sk_strike_1 inside the rule premise rather than variables, so the premise can only match those exact symbols — which nothing ever asserts — and the general 'whenever cold wind strikes the Cliff Path at night' reading collapses into a claim about one particular unasserted striking.
The consequent's Skolem event (sk_go_out $x) is a function of the lantern alone, so nothing relates a lantern's going-out to the striking occasion that the conditional makes it depend on.

q2_gaps: indicative conditional 'If <event clause>, <generic clause>' — the instruction set says only that it is a plain Implication rule and shows no worked example, so nothing fixes whether the antecedent clause's event and participants must be rule variables (vs. witness constants), nor whether the consequent's per-occurrence event links back to the antecedent occasion
review_run1.notes: The proper-noun handling ('Cliff Path' → one opaque symbol + Name + (Member cliff_path path), no modifier genus), the phrasal verb kept whole as go_out with no genus, the change-of-state Patient on the lantern, the positive treatment of the un- adjective 'unprepared', and the bare day-part (Time … night) are all correct.

fields.sentence: Lanterns in shielded coves stay safe from cold winds.

q1_issues.issue: The bare plural 'cold winds' is given a specific witness sk_wind_1 asserted at TOP LEVEL, so a generic sentence asserts that a particular cold wind exists; an oblique's bare (article-less) plural should stay the kind constant, and the singular witness also collapses the plural.
(Member sk_wind_1 cold) predicates 'cold' of that invented singular witness rather than of the kind the text names, compounding the same over-assertion.

q2_gaps: a stative linking verb + adjective ('stay/remain safe'): the instruction set covers only 'be' copulas plus become/turn change-of-state and the postural/locative statives, so it does not say whether 'stay safe' reifies a 'stay' event or is a plain copular predication — here the verb is silently dropped

a modified bare-plural kind as an oblique filler ('safe from cold winds'): the oblique-object rule gives only 'article mints a witness / bare mass, domain, proper name stays a constant', with no form for a bare plural carrying a descriptive adjective

a kind-level property claim restricted by an NP-internal locative PP ('lanterns in shielded coves'): both the ConditionalProperty locative-restriction rule and the restrictive-modifier-in-rule-premises form are licensed and nothing disambiguates them
review_run1.notes: The reified state (Member/Experiencer) + surface-preposition oblique + retained flat (Member $x safe) is exactly the adjective-PP-complement pattern, and the restriction is kept in the rule premises rather than stripped. The defect is entirely in how the complement NP was individuated.
